requirements: No hover casting over absent or invisible party/pet/target/raid slots
Handle party join/leave, party-to-raid and raid-to-party, unit reassignment and disappearance during combat
Hide the detached separator/atlas when the owner or group ancestor is hidden; preserve appearance and responsive active casting
Keep protected operations on prepared native secure handlers; no ordinary combat registration or frame mutation

causes: Detached separator initialized from local IsShown although its group ancestor was hidden; Build Hide then produced no effective OnHide transition
Secure setup-bindings accepted nonexistent/invisible unit surfaces; visual scan also admitted locally shown frames below hidden ancestors
Secure unit assignment could change without OnLeave; prior mouseover-exists cleanup retained missing sources based solely on hovered geometry
implementation: Detached separator and atlas initialization/OnShow use effective IsVisible; separator explicitly disables mouse input
Shared secure valid-hover snippet resolves the current unit on the surface or its parent chain and verifies effective visibility/UnitExists
Preinstalled secure OnAttributeChanged wrappers clear or rearm owner/child bindings on unit changes, including a remembered real enter under a stationary cursor
Mouseover-exists cleanup checks the actual source unit; leave/hide retires remembered enter ownership
Mouse-focus attribution and geometric scans reject frames below hidden ancestors
combatMechanism: Prepared secure wrappers/RunFor run from native dispatch in combat. Existing roster visibility drivers remain unchanged. No new driver/ticker/roster poll or ordinary protected write is added.

contracts: RestrictedEnvironment exposes UnitExists; UnitExists declares a plain bool with no secret return annotation in inspected sources
RestrictedFrames.RunFor returns the restricted closure result; GetAttribute/GetParent resolve handles rather than ordinary native fields
SecureHandlers permits OnAttributeChanged wrapping; our unit-change wrapper does not return false or suppress the original native callback
